notes:
Specifically refers to the hard dorsal shell of turtles, tortoises, and crabs. Also used in the set expression {甲羅|こうら}{干|ぼ}し, meaning a turtle basking in the sun on a rock.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {甲羅|こうら}{干|ぼ}し: sunbathing (said of turtles)
- ⟦{亀|かめ}→亀：02198_kame⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{甲羅|こうら}: turtle shell
- カニ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{甲羅|こうら}: crab shell
- {甲羅|こうら}{焼|や}き: grilled in the shell (a crab dish)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{殻|から}→殻：02148_kara⟧: shell — broader, includes eggs, nuts, and shellfish
- ⟦{貝殻|かいがら}→貝殻：19457_kaigara⟧: seashell — specifically the shell of a bivalve or snail

ETYMOLOGY:
The kanji {甲|こう} means "shell" or "armor" and {羅|ら} contributes a covering sense, together describing the armored shell.

definitions.explanation: the hard outer shell of a turtle, tortoise, or crab; a carapace
